title_prefix: Amounts render as JSON doubles instead o
mechanism: Core's ValueFromAmount (refs/bitcoin/src/core_io.cpp:285-296 at d3056bc) builds a UniValue of type VNUM whose raw text is strprintf("%s%d.%08d", sign, quotient, remainder) -- always exactly eight decimal places -- and UniValue writes that stored text out verbatim, so every BTC field is a JSON number token with a fixed 8-decimal spelling. Our satoshi->btc (src/rpc/amounts.lisp:63-65) returns (/ satoshis 100000000.0d0), a double-float, and yason:encode prints it with SBCL's shortest-round-trip float printer. Every amount site in the tree is double: `grep -rn "100000000\.0" src/` finds 39 occurrences and all 39 are the d0 form, with 22 of them going through satoshi->btc, so no single-float path exists (that matters -- yason renders the single-float 1e-8 as 0.00000000999999993922529).
consequence: Presentation only, and that is the point of executing it rather than assuming. A 243,002-value sweep over the whole MoneyRange found ZERO cases where the emitted token is not a plain decimal (never exponent form, never an SBCL 'd' exponent marker, so the document stays valid JSON) and ZERO cases where the token, parsed exactly as a decimal, differs from Core's fixed-8 value. The difference is always and only trailing zeros: 0 sat -> 0.0 vs 0.00000000, 1000 -> 0.00001 vs 0.00001000, 100000000 -> 1.0 vs 1.00000000, 5000000000 -> 50.0 vs 50.00000000, 2099999997690000 -> 20999999.9769 vs 20999999.97690000, -1000 -> -0.00001 vs -0.00001000; where the value needs all eight digits the two agree character for character (1 -> 0.00000001, 12345678 -> 0.12345678, 2099999999999999 -> 20999999.99999999, the largest in-range satoshi count). Precision only fails ABOVE MoneyRange -- 9007199254740993 sat renders as 90071992.54740992, one satoshi short -- and no valid chain can produce such an amount. So Core's own assert_equal on Decimal values passes, a client's JSON number parse is unaffected, and only raw-text comparison or a byte diff against a Core reply sees it. S3, not S2.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3c, warm image. probe5.lisp printed yason:encode of (bl.rpc::satoshi->btc s) beside Core's (format nil "~D.~8,'0D") for 20 boundary values (0, 1, 10, 1000, 100000, 21000000, 100000000, 12345678, 99999999, 2099999997690000, 2100000000000000, 2099999999999999, -1000, -1, 5000000000, and three out-of-range controls). probe6.lisp then swept 243,002 amounts -- 200,000 random in [0, 21e6 BTC], 20,000 random sub-BTC, 20,000 random negatives, every satoshi in [2099999999999000, 2100000000000000], and 0..2000 -- encoding each with yason and parsing the token back as an EXACT rational: result 'checked=243002 exponent-form=0 value-mismatch=0'. Positive control (probe7.lisp) for that checker: the out-of-range 9007199254740993 sat is caught as a value mismatch (90071992.54740992 vs 90071992.54740993), 4611686018427387904 sat is caught, and a single-float 1e-8 is caught by the exponent/decimal parse. Ours: src/rpc/amounts.lisp:63-65 (satoshi->btc), src/rpc/server.lisp:340-355 (rpc-result->json) and :1123 (yason:encode of the reply). Core at d3056bc: core_io.cpp:285-296. Core functional tests read these fields as Decimal (rpc_rawtransaction.py:225 asserts isinstance(gottx['fee'], Decimal)), which is exactly why the divergence is invisible to them.
fix_shape: Emit the amount as a JSON number TOKEN whose text is Core's, instead of letting a float printer choose the spelling. Add a raw-number wrapper the encoder understands -- a small struct or a (:json-number . "string") marker that rpc-result->json passes through and that a yason:encode method (or the existing writer) prints verbatim without quotes -- and make satoshi->btc return that wrapper built by the FormatMoney-style integer path already in this file (format-money at src/rpc/amounts.lisp:77-86 is nearly it; the amount form keeps all eight digits instead of trimming, and the sign must come from the sign of the satoshi count so that -0.00001000 prints with its minus). Change satoshi->btc alone and all 22 call sites follow; the 17 remaining raw (/ x 100000000.0d0) expressions, including the fee field at src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:467, the prevout value at :494-496 and the gettxout value at :718, should be routed through it in the same pass so no amount keeps the double path. Non-amount doubles (difficulty, feerates in BTC/kvB that Core also formats through ValueFromAmount, verificationprogress) must be audited individually rather than blanket-converted. A regression test should assert the exact token for 0, 1, 1000, 100000000 and 2099999999999999 satoshis, plus a negative, and a positive control that the wrapper is not being quoted as a string.
